points.why: It says the net-total fit can't separate the two stories and warns that a flattening curve is easy to fit with several free parameters.
It audits each model's assumptions and counts free parameters, but never proposes link-by-link review with sales or support staff or with reviewers who built neither model.
It gives many discriminating checks (adds vs churn, churn by support contact, timing, segments, funnel) and asks each analyst to name in advance what result would prove them wrong.
It reasons about the expansion-vs-support decision through asymmetry, reversibility and a pilot, but never tests which uncertain parameters would flip the choice.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly says fit can't discriminate and never picks the better-fitting model.
